comparisons.peer_summary: Cash dividends declared on preferred stock were $1.6 billion in each of 2024, 2023, and 2022. In 2024, the Corporation fully redeemed Series X, Series U, Series JJ, and Series Z stock at their liquidation preference values for a total of $5.3 billion.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America actively redeemed fixed-to-floating rate non-cumulative preferred stock in 2024, though they redeemed different series. JPMorgan redeemed Series Q, R, S, U, FF, X, and HH (with redemptions occurring between April 2024 and February 2025) totaling $12.9 billion, while Bank of America fully redeemed Series X, U, JJ, and Z during 2024 totaling $5.3 billion. Both firms used liquidation preference values for these redemptions.

sentences.text: On October 1, 2024, the Firm redeemed all $1.6 billion of its fixed-to-floating rate non-cumulative preferred stock, Series X.
On April 30, 2024, the Firm redeemed all $1.0 billion of its fixed-to-floating rate non-cumulative preferred stock, Series U.
During 2024, the Corporation fully redeemed Series X, Series U, Series JJ and Series Z stock at their liquidation preference values for a total of $5.3 billion.

peer_results.rationale: Citi's candidate disclosures relate to the issuance of new Series FF preferred stock in 2025 and the dividend terms/redemption of Series V in 2025, rather than redemptions occurring during the 2024 fiscal year comparable to JPMorgan's 2024 redemptions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Redemption of Series K and Series P Preferred Stock in 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, the firm redeemed all outstanding shares of its Series K Preferred Stock ($700 million value) and Series P Preferred Stock ($1.50 billion value), recording a $34 million difference between redemption value and net carrying value as an addition to preferred stock dividends.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs redeemed Series K and Series P Preferred Stock in 2024, recording a $34 million difference between redemption value and net carrying value as an addition to preferred stock dividends. In contrast, JPMorgan's redemption disclosures for 2024 (e.g., Series FF, X, Q, R, S, U) and early 2025 (Series HH) do not mention any gain or loss on redemption or adjustments to carrying value, focusing solely on the extinguishment of the specific series and amounts.

sentences.text: On August 1, 2024, the Firm redeemed all $2.3 billion of its fixed-to-floating rate non-cumulative preferred stock, Series FF.
On October 1, 2024, the Firm redeemed all $1.6 billion of its fixed-to-floating rate non-cumulative preferred stock, Series X.
On February 1, 2025, the Firm redeemed all $3.0 billion of its fixed-to-floating rate non-cumulative preferred stock, Series HH.
On May 1, 2024, the Firm redeemed all $5.0 billion of its fixed-to-floating rate non-cumulative preferred stock, Series Q, Series R and Series S.

In 2024, the firm redeemed all outstanding shares of its (i) Series K 6.375% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock (Series K Preferred Stock) with a redemption value of $700 million ($25,000 per share), plus accrued and unpaid dividends and (ii) Series P 5.00% Fixed-to-Floating Rate Non-Cumulative Preferred Stock (Series P Preferred Stock) with a redemption value of $1.50 billion ($25,000 per share), plus accrued and unpaid dividends.
The difference between the redemption value and net carrying value at the time of these redemptions was $34 million, which was recorded as an addition to preferred stock dividends in 2024.

peer_results.rationale: Morgan Stanley's candidate disclosures concern general dividend rate structures for various series and the historical issuance of Series P in 2022, rather than specific 2024 preferred stock redemptions.
